problem: Diffusion/flow-based multimodal models suffer from slow generation speeds and high computational costs, limiting deployment in resource-constrained real-time applications.
approach: LaTtE-Flow introduces a layer-wise timestep-expert architecture that distributes flow-matching across specialized groups of transformer layers, each handling a distinct subset of timesteps, combined with timestep-conditioned residual attention for efficient information reuse.
contribution: Achieves around 6× faster inference speed compared to recent unified multimodal models while maintaining competitive image generation quality.

problem: Sample-wise reward functions in visual generative model training cause reward hacking, leading to mode collapse and visual anomalies that degrade image diversity.
approach: Uses distribution-wise rewards that account for data distribution across samples rather than individual samples, with a subset-replace strategy for efficient reward estimation and RL-based post-hoc model merging optimization.
contribution: Improves FID-50K from 8.30 to 5.77 for SiT and 3.74 to 3.52 for EDM2 while enhancing perceptual quality and preserving sample diversity.

problem: Gromov-Wasserstein distance computation suffers from cubic time complexity O(n³), which severely limits scalability for large-scale structured data alignment.
approach: LoBCD-GW reveals data-dependent sparsity in coupling matrix updates and introduces a localized block coordinate selection strategy that confines optimization to a selected set of size r much less than n, achieving O(r³) complexity.
contribution: Achieves 5.8× speedup on large-scale graph alignment benchmarks while maintaining state-of-the-art accuracy.

problem: Standard RL methods for LLM-as-a-Judge use binary rewards, ignoring ordinal structure in regression tasks and failing to recognize that near-correct predictions are better than far-wrong ones.
approach: REAL reformulates LLM scoring as regression-aware RL using generalized policy gradient estimation, decomposing optimization into chain-of-thought exploration and regression-aware prediction refinement.
contribution: Achieves +8.40 Pearson and +7.20 Spearman correlation gains over SFT baseline on Qwen3-32B with significantly better out-of-domain generalization.

problem: Neural Granger causality methods rely on simple local measures for causal discovery that extract only partial information from complex models and may miss global dependencies.
approach: Reformulates Granger causality as a feature attribution problem using Information-Theoretic Shapley values to measure global feature importance, with novel regularizers to suppress spurious relationships and mitigate overfitting.
contribution: Demonstrates robust causal relationship recovery on synthetic and realistic datasets with flexible model-agnostic regularizers that can integrate into any differentiable neural network.

problem: Gradient compression in distributed optimization degrades convergence guarantees, yet error feedback mechanisms lack unified understanding of their relative performance and convergence properties.
approach: Provides tight convergence analyses for Error Feedback (EF) and Error Feedback 21 (EF21) methods by identifying optimal step-size choices and constructing optimal Lyapunov functions tailored to each algorithm.
contribution: Recovers known best guarantees possible in single-agent regime with convergence analysis independent of the number of agents.

problem: Infrared-visible image fusion in Euclidean space imposes rigid distance metrics that distort multi-modal interactions and hierarchical semantic structures.
approach: Introduces text-driven fusion framework using hyperbolic geometry where BLIP-extracted text prompts serve as topological anchors, enabling hierarchical semantic embeddings through the Poincaré ball's negative curvature.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art fusion approaches on benchmark datasets with autonomous content-aware adaptation at inference time without requiring textual input.

problem: Current generalized category discovery methods focus on clustering objectives while overlooking that standard vision backbones produce high-rank, entangled token representations unsuitable for discovering latent concepts.
approach: Proposes Compositional Primitive Fields (CPF-GCD) that enforce low-rank compositional organization in feature space, decomposing images into reusable atomic visual primitives and their spatial layouts.
contribution: Provides a generic plug-and-play module that consistently boosts performance across diverse GCD baselines by explicitly modeling spatial distribution of primitives.

problem: Automatic introduction generation for scientific papers demands logical soundness and verifiable faithfulness but is treated as text generation, leading to hallucinated citations and incoherent reasoning.
approach: LECTOR formulates content-conditional introduction generation task and proposes Logic-Expression Co-Reinforcement Learning framework that constructs logic-reasoning graphs and jointly optimizes structural fidelity and narrative quality.
contribution: Demonstrates improvements on Nature Communications papers: Graph Quality +26.7%, Citation Quality +8.6%, and Paper Consistency +3.3%.

problem: Text-to-3D generation models struggle with coarse semantic alignment and lack robust 3D spatial understanding, resulting in geometric inconsistencies and catastrophic failures in part assembly.
approach: VLM3D repurposes vision-language models as differentiable semantic and spatial critics using dual-query critic signals derived from VLM Yes/No log-odds to assess both semantic fidelity and geometric coherence.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods on standard benchmarks while actively steering sampling processes to correct severe spatial errors in both optimization-based and feed-forward 3D generation pipelines.

problem: Internal reasoning mechanisms in large language models remain underexplored, and supervised approaches relying on human-defined concepts fail to capture the full spectrum of reasoning behaviors.
approach: RISE proposes unsupervised discovery of reasoning vectors using sparse auto-encoders trained on step-level chain-of-thought activations to uncover disentangled features encoding distinct reasoning behaviors.
contribution: Discovers interpretable behaviors like reflection and backtracking with targeted interventions enabling controllable amplification or suppression of specific reasoning behaviors without retraining.

problem: Multimodal verification systems lack fine-grained error localization and robust verification mechanisms to support safer deployment of foundation models.
approach: OmniVerifier-M1 uses symbolic meta-verification outputs (bounding boxes) as verifier rationales with decoupled reinforcement learning objectives for binary judgment and meta-verification, enabling rule-based reward computation.
contribution: Provides robust verification and fine-grained error localization, enabling M1-TTS verifier-driven system for dynamic region-level self-correction.

problem: Text-to-Image models perpetuate and amplify societal biases, with existing evaluation methods addressing only single-dimensional biases and lacking multidimensional fairness analysis.
approach: HoloFair introduces comprehensive fairness benchmark with SpaFreq attribute classifier and Multi-attribute Group-wise Bias Index metric, plus Fair-GRPO reinforcement learning debiasing with multi-objective reward function.
contribution: Fair-GRPO significantly improves multidimensional fairness on SD3.5-Medium while maintaining high image quality with analysis of reward hacking mitigation.

problem: KL constraints in RL for LLMs over-penalize low-probability actions and lack sparsity to discard marginal policy shifts, limiting effective exploration.
approach: MRPO enforces L1-norm constraints on policy updates instead of KL constraints, which is more tolerant of low-probability actions yet strictly suppresses minor probability perturbations.
contribution: Doubles GRPO performance gains in preference alignment, outperforms DAPO in mathematical reasoning, and surpasses DPO in offline settings using only binary rewards with monotonic improvement guarantees.

problem: Language models coupled to external tokenizers lack end-to-end raw-byte training, limiting inference-time flexibility and robustness while maintaining separate model and compression pipelines.
approach: Proxy compression jointly trains models on raw byte sequences and compressed views, allowing internal alignment between formats through transfer learning that enables inference on raw bytes.
contribution: Substantially improves training efficiency on code language modeling and outperforms pure byte-level baselines at fixed compute budgets, eventually matching tokenizer approaches while retaining byte-level robustness.

problem: Continuous ECG monitoring scaling to contactless mmWave sensing is severely constrained by scarcity of high-quality synchronized recordings.
approach: Cardio-mmFlow uses Gaussian-prior-free physics-informed flow matching to synthesize mmWave radar signals from clinical ECG, learning direct transport trajectory between ECG and radar latent manifolds with subject-dependent modulation.
contribution: Generates high-fidelity radar data enabling zero-shot downstream mmWave to ECG reconstruction and Atrial Fibrillation classification with synthetic data.

problem: Multimodal continual learning exhibits both semantic relation drift and hierarchy-related distortion under hyperbolic geometry, whose behavior under continual learning remains underexplored.
approach: Establishes theoretical foundation showing forgetting requires cross-modal invariance under shared hyperbolic isometry, guiding principled framework that preserves geometric structure while adapting to new tasks.
contribution: Demonstrates effective approach on continual multimodal benchmarks that preserves essential geometric structure and hierarchical geometry while enabling task adaptation.

problem: Neural Controlled Differential Equations restrict efficiency due to roughness of driving control paths that force adaptive solvers to take excessively small steps.
approach: Replaces exact spline interpolation with Kernel and Gaussian Process smoothing for explicit trajectory regularity control, employing attention-based Multi-View CDE using learnable queries to recover lost details.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while significantly reducing Number of Function Evaluations and total inference time compared to spline-based baselines.

problem: Diffusion Transformers for real-world image super-resolution have heavy inference burden hindering deployment, and existing PTQ methods designed for text-to-image tasks lead to severe local texture degradation.
approach: Q-DiT4SR proposes hierarchical SVD integrating global low-rank branch with local block-wise rank-1 branch, plus variance-aware spatiotemporal mixed-precision allocating cross-layer weight and intra-layer activation precision via dynamic programming.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance under W4A6 and W4A4 settings with 5.8× model size reduction and 6.14× computational operation reduction.

problem: Online RL for LLMs exhibits imbalanced exploration-exploitation trade-off, resulting in unstable optimization with suboptimal performance.
approach: IB-TPO formulates Information Bottleneck-Score as fine-grained optimization objective using novel IB-guided tree sampling strategy that improves efficiency and reuses tree structure for effective Monte Carlo estimation.
contribution: Significantly outperforms GRPO baseline by 2.9% to 3.6% and other state-of-the-art approaches with 50% more trajectories under same token budget.

problem: Flow-matching Q-functions in RL are effective but their advantages remain unclear compared to standard critics, and the mechanisms enabling their success are unexplained.
approach: Shows flow-matching Q-functions couple learned velocity field with integration procedure enabling test-time recovery from imperfect estimates where errors dampen out, and induce plastic representations for non-stationary TD targets.
contribution: Flow-matching critics outperform monolithic critics by over 2× in performance and achieve 5-10× higher sample efficiency in high-UTD regimes.

problem: Audio-Visual LLMs face prohibitive computational costs processing massive redundant tokens, and positional encoding causes aliasing when sparse sampling violates the Nyquist limit.
approach: EchoingPixels uses Cross-Modal Semantic Sieve for joint audio-visual token extraction with dynamic budget allocation, plus Sync-RoPE spectral low-pass filter adapting rotary positional embeddings bandwidth to sparse sampling rate.
contribution: Achieves performance comparable to full models using only 5-20% of original tokens while preserving temporal monotonicity.

problem: Sleep medicine remains restricted to task-specific models focusing on localized micro-structure features while neglecting rich multi-modal polysomnography context and global sleep architecture.
approach: SleepMaMi uses hierarchical dual-encoder design with Macro-Encoder trained via Demographic-Guided Contrastive Learning for full-night patterns and Micro-Encoder optimized via hybrid MAE and multi-modal contrastive learning.
contribution: Trained on over 20,000 PSG recordings (158K hours), outperforms or matches existing foundation models across diverse downstream tasks with superior generalizability.

problem: Offline MBRL follows two-stage procedure causing objective mismatch where world models optimize likelihood rather than policy learning, and policies lack robustness to adversarial noise.
approach: Proposes maximin optimization framework that dynamically adapts world model alongside policy using unified objective aimed at robustness improvement, solved via Stackelberg learning dynamics.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on twelve noisy D4RL MuJoCo tasks and three stochastic Tokamak Control tasks with theoretical analysis supporting the design.

problem: Asset allocation separates forecasting from optimization, creating fundamental mismatch where minimizing prediction errors fails to yield robust portfolios.
approach: Signature Informed Transformer unifies feature extraction and decision making through path signatures to encode complex dependencies, specialized attention amplifying geometric asset relationships, and direct CVaR minimization.
contribution: Significantly outperforms both traditional strategies and advanced forecasting baselines across diverse equity universes.

problem: Model-based RL suffers from unstable training due to dynamics model learning mismatch where models trained on historical policy data are queried under continually updated policy.
approach: PMER proposes lightweight replay mechanism prioritizing high-error transitions during dynamics model training, implicitly emphasizing policy-relevant regions without explicit policy distance estimation.
contribution: Improves stability, faster convergence, and higher sample efficiency on MuJoCo benchmarks based on finite-horizon performance analysis decomposing policy gaps.

problem: Existing camouflaged object detection approaches rely on multiple diffusion steps to refine masks, which is computationally expensive.
approach: CODiff reformulates diffusion process for one-step mask prediction with global semantic guidance and hierarchical condition integration blocks for fine-grained structural semantics.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance with over 22% MAE improvement on challenging COD10K dataset using one-step inference.

problem: Knowledge distillation effectiveness depends on intertwined choices of divergence direction and optimization strategy, and existing methods struggle to balance mode coverage and mode-seeking behaviors.
approach: HPD integrates complementary advantages of forward and reverse KL with hybrid approach combining off-policy data with lightweight approximate on-policy sampling at token level.
contribution: Demonstrates improved optimization stability, computational efficiency, and final performance across diverse model families and scales on math reasoning, dialogue, and code tasks.

problem: Real-world graph datasets arise from mixtures of populations with distinct underlying distributions, but standard methods treat graphs as homogeneous.
approach: Proposes unified graphon-mixture framework representing graphs as samples from probabilistic graphon mixture models, using graph moments to cluster and estimate graphon components.
contribution: Develops GMAM for graph mixup augmentation and MGCL for contrastive learning, achieving new SOTA on six of seven supervised datasets and competitive performance on unsupervised benchmarks.

problem: Learning in partially observable Markov games against strategic adaptive opponents requires understanding latent dynamics from partial observations with unknown adversary behavior.
approach: Epoch-based optimistic maximum-likelihood algorithm selects policies per geometrically growing epoch using confidence sets, keeping policy comparison cost logarithmic in horizon.
contribution: Achieves Õ(√T) policy regret with explicit dependence on horizon, adversary memory, and aggregate Eluder dimension, matched by lower bound up to logarithmic factors.

problem: Dynamic graphs exhibit diverse time-evolving topologies but existing methods embed into single curvature space, limiting representation quality when geometry misaligns with local topology.
approach: DyGMoCE incorporates mixture-of-experts to attention and feed-forward modules where each expert operates on distinct Riemannian manifold curvature, with ranking-constrained routing and fast Riemannian attention module.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods with average 27.5% speedup and 52.6% memory reduction from fast Riemannian attention applicable to general Transformer models.

problem: Hallucination detection in LLMs remains less effective on reasoning tasks despite strong performance on question-answering.
approach: Reframes hallucination detection as out-of-distribution detection problem, treating next-token prediction as classification with training-free single-sample based detectors.
contribution: Achieves strong accuracy in hallucination detection on reasoning tasks, suggesting OOD detection provides scalable pathway toward language model safety.

problem: High load variability in LLM serving leads to significant GPU under-utilization that existing systems fail to exploit.
approach: ConServe enables fine-grained resource sharing through latency-aware token-level scheduling, sub-iteration layer-wise preemption, and incremental KV-cache management for co-serving online and offline tasks.
contribution: Improves throughput by 2.2× on average and reduces online tail latency by 2.9× over state-of-the-art systems on Llama-3.1 and Qwen-2.5.

problem: Activation steering effectiveness depends on empirical heuristics for intervention location and parameterization lacking principled foundation.
approach: Establishes first-order equivalence between activation-space interventions and weight-space updates, deriving conditions for activation steering to replicate fine-tuning with joint adaptation training in both spaces simultaneously.
contribution: Achieves accuracy within 0.2%-0.9% of full-parameter tuning on average across tasks and models while training only 0.04% of parameters, outperforming ReFT and LoRA.

problem: LLM alignment methods are vulnerable to significant noise prevalent in real-world preference datasets, degrading performance.
approach: Introduces theoretical framework with Unbiased Reward Model loss and Unbiased Direct Preference Optimization loss that mathematically correct distortion induced by preference noise.
contribution: Demonstrates noise-tolerant, parameter downward compatible methods that outperform state-of-the-art baselines across diverse datasets with rigorous theoretical analyses.

problem: Existing error slice discovery methods generate explanations disconnected from model inference, only approximating error sources and producing inaccurate explanations.
approach: CB-SLICE leverages Concept Bottleneck Models whose predictions depend directly on semantic concepts, grouping samples with shared concept prediction failures and identifying responsible concept keywords.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods in uncovering well-known biases while providing richer and more faithful explanations directly linked to error sources.

problem: Low-rank constraints in federated LoRA fine-tuning exacerbate noise sensitivity, leading to overfitting and aggregation bias in noisy federated scenarios.
approach: FedDR-LoRA decouples robust feature learning from noise modeling using dual-branch mechanism where down-projection matrix A learns stable features and up-projection matrix B models noise with negative learning.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various noisy federated scenarios by establishing global consensus through aggregating B while preserving local feature alignment.

problem: Piecewise stationary bandits without knowledge of underlying non-stationarity require methods that work across common variants without prior knowledge of change patterns.
approach: DAL introduces practical black-box framework accepting any stationary bandit algorithm and augmenting it with change detector, enabling applicability to all common bandit variants.
contribution: Consistently surpasses all state-of-the-art methods across diverse non-stationary scenarios including synthetic benchmarks and real-world datasets with theoretical insights.

problem: Multi-instance partial-label learning struggles because relationships between key instances and ground-truth labels are heavily covered by false positive labels.
approach: AGOPMIPL computes average gradient outer product directly from bag features and model predictions, integrating into attention module to amplify discriminative directions with feature prototypes and progressive disambiguation strategy.
contribution: Consistently outperforms five state-of-the-art baselines across four MIPL benchmarks with up to 25.9% relative gain on real-world CRC-MIPL dataset.

problem: Diffusion policies achieve remarkable robotic manipulation success but often fail to satisfy strict physical constraints required for safe real-world deployment.
approach: PACT proposes self-evolving post-training framework projecting pretrained policies onto constraint-feasible regions via constraint-gradient distillation with curriculum progressively tightening constraints.
contribution: Reduces safety violations by 31.0% on average while improving task success by 30.7% on simulated and real-world embodied manipulation benchmarks.
